title: Father of flame and the carrier of firewood
translation: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he! His wealth and all he earned will not help him. He will burn in a fire of flame, and his wife too, carrier of firewood, with a rope of palm fibre around her neck.
body: The nickname **Abū Lahab**, “father of flame”, returns as the **“fire of flame”** of verse 3. Early exegetes split on verse 4: **Ibn ʿAbbās** saw his wife strewing thorns; **Mujāhid** and **Qatāda** read “carrying firewood” as **spreading slander**. Proverbs uses that image; Luther’s Small Catechism: don’t slander, defend your neighbour.
question: Nickname, fire, firewood, rope: each image answers another. What might this matching say about how the surah pictures judgement?
source_label: Mawdudi, Tafhim al-Qur’an on Surah 111 · Small Catechism, Eighth Commandment
reading: Uri Rubin, “Abū Lahab and Sūra CXI”, BSOAS 42 (1979)
